title: Day Clocks for Parents and Grandparents: Two Options That Spell Out the Date
subtitle: A plain-English look at clocks that show the full day, date and time in whole words, what two of them cost and what to check before you give one.
excerpt: Day clocks spell out the day of the week, the date and the time with no abbreviations. Here is what two of them offer, what to check first and what they cost, at $59.95 and $69.95.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: It is easy to lose track of the day now and then. For some older adults, being unsure whether it is Tuesday or Saturday, morning or evening, happens often enough to be a worry. Abbreviations like "WED 11/4" can add to the confusion.

A day clock is a simple answer. It is a digital display that shows the day of the week, the date and the time in whole words, so there is nothing to decode. For a parent or grandparent who has low vision or who gets mixed up about the date, it can be a practical, low-fuss gift.
Think of it as a large screen that does one job. Instead of "WED 11/4," it writes out "Wednesday" and "November" in full. The MindCare clock below also shows the part of the day.

Beyond that, the two clocks in this article differ. The MindCare model has five alarms for wake-ups, medication reminders and appointments, and adjustable brightness with day and night modes. The American Lifetime page does not mention alarms or brightness controls. Both can display eight languages, including English and Spanish.

It is worth being clear about what these clocks cannot do. They show the day, date and time, and the MindCare model adds alarms. They do not treat or slow memory loss. They are not a voice assistant or a video-call display, and they are not a medical alert device, so they cannot call for help. If you are worried about a loved one's memory, their doctor is the right person to talk to. In an emergency, call 911.

items: Full words, no abbreviations. This is the whole point. Check that the day and month are spelled out completely.
Screen size and contrast. Both clocks below have 8-inch screens. MindCare says its text is bright white or warm white on a black background.
Brightness control. MindCare lists adjustable brightness with day and night modes. American Lifetime's page does not say, so ask before buying if that matters to you.
Power and backup. Both clocks plug into a wall outlet, so the display may go dark in a power cut. Neither page confirms battery backup.

Alarms and reminders. If you want medication or appointment reminders, the alarms are fixed and basic, so someone has to set them up. MindCare's page does not say whether a person needs to program them, so confirm that with the seller before gifting.
Where it will go. Both can sit on a surface or be mounted on a wall. MindCare includes a stand.

Fees, shipping and returns. Neither clock mentions a monthly fee. American Lifetime lists free shipping on all orders. MindCare's banner says orders over $40 ship free in the continental US, with no sales tax. American Lifetime's page does not state a warranty or return policy, and MindCare's return policy is not given in what we have, so ask both before buying, especially for a gift.

sections.content: Two day clocks worth a look
Both of these are 8-inch clocks sold by American Lifetime and by MindCare Store, a memory-care retailer. Prices were checked on November 3, 2026.
Setting it up and using it well
Setup on the MindCare clock is meant to be simple. The store describes it as plug and play.
"Simply plug it in and your Day Clock will display the time and date." (MindCare Store product page)

Even so, it can help if the gift-giver handles the first setup. Choose the language and, on the MindCare model, pick 12-hour or 24-hour time and set the brightness. If you plan to use the reminder alarms, first confirm with MindCare how they are programmed. Then write down what each one is for, since the person receiving the clock may not want to fiddle with buttons.
Keep the clock near an outlet, since both models plug in. Put it somewhere it will be seen often during the day.

A day clock can feel like a hint that someone is slipping. Present it gently, as a handy, easy-to-read calendar clock. MindCare says its screen can be seen from up to 20 feet away by people with vision impairment.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A good gift does not have to be complicated. A clear clock that quietly answers "What day is it?" can save a few small frustrations. Check the warranty and return policy, set it up before you hand it over, and give it with a smile.

products.name: American Lifetime Day Clock (8")
products.blurb: A straightforward choice for someone who mainly needs the day, date and time spelled out in bold, clear words, in black or white. It sits on a desk or counter or mounts on a wall, and offers 8 display languages.

products.name: MindCare Store Day & Date Calendar Clock w/ Reminders (MC-0045)
products.blurb: Suits someone who could use reminders as well as the date, with 5 alarms for wake-ups, medication or appointments. The 8-inch LED screen shows the part of the day and has adjustable brightness with day and night modes.
